subject: Re: ZenPath DPA — definition and execution for training prohibition (DocuSign)
messages:
From: Marcus Li <marcus.li@zenpath.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>; laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: ZenPath Legal <legal@zenpath.ai>; Aisha Kapoor <aisha@zenpath.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: DPA redline: absolute prohibition on model training

Vivek / Laura —

Thanks for taking the time on the call today. As discussed, ZenPath needs an explicit, broad prohibition in the DPA preventing Redwood from using any Customer Data for model training or model improvement. Our legal team is sensitive about any potential downstream inclusion of our PII or proprietary logs in your training corpora.

Key asks from our side:
- Add clause: “Provider shall not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any models or datasets, whether internal or external.”
- Define “Customer Data” to include logs, transcripts, and derived metrics tied to customer identifiers.
- Prohibit transfers of Customer Data to subprocessors located outside the US without prior written consent.

Attached: our annotated DPA with examples (ZenPath_DPA_redlines_v2.docx). We are prepared to execute quickly via DocuSign if you can accept these redlines or provide a clear alternative carve-out language that gives equivalent protections.

Regards,
Marcus
Head of Security Operations
ZenPath AI

--

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Li <marcus.li@zenpath.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, rafael_mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 12:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA redline: absolute prohibition on model training

Marcus —

Appreciate the clear summary and the redlines. We absolutely prioritize customer data protections and want to get this across the finish line. A few notes from our side to propose a workable path forward (high-level):

1) We can accept a prohibition on using Customer Data for model training that is narrowly scoped to “training for public or shared models.” However, we need an operational carve allowing us to use aggregated, de-identified signals for platform diagnostics, bug fixes, and quality monitoring. This is standard for running a reliable inference service.

2) Definitions: let’s align on the exact language for “Customer Data” vs. “Derived Data” vs. “Model Improvements.” We propose the following:
   - Customer Data: raw inputs (requests), attachments, and associated metadata tied to Customer accounts.
   - Derived Data: aggregated, pseudonymized metrics that cannot be reverse-engineered to identify an individual or account.
   - Model Improvements: changes to model weights trained on datasets that may include public corpora and non-customer training data.

3) Subprocessors and transfers: we can commit to restrict any model-training activity involving Customer Data to US-only subprocessors and require notice + opt-in for cross-border training. For routine infra subprocessors (monitoring, logging), we can provide the subprocessor list and an update process.

Can your legal team review a short proposed alternate paragraph? If acceptable, we’ll turn it into a DocuSign envelope today.

Thanks — Vivek
VP, Product & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

>
> Thanks for taking the time on the call today. As discussed, ZenPath needs an explicit, broad prohibition in the DPA preventing Redwood from using any Customer Data for model training or model improvement.

Vivek —

We reviewed your proposed carve-out language. ZenPath can consider a limited exception for operational, non-training uses, but we need the following guardrails to be contractually explicit:

- Any use of pseudonymized or aggregated data must be certified by an independent privacy review and subject to a documented process;
- Derived Data may not be used to train or evaluate models that are deployed outside of Redwood’s isolated customer environments;
- We require a 30-day notice and written consent for adding any new subprocessor that could access Customer Data, and express prohibition on using Customer Data in any cross-border model training without prior consent.

Please redline the exact paragraph you propose (we prefer short, tight language). If acceptable, we will sign via DocuSign.

Thanks,

Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed DPA paragraph and operational commitments

Hi all —

Following up with the short paragraph we discussed. Please review and confirm whether it meets ZenPath’s contract objectives; if yes, we will push to DocuSign this afternoon.

Proposed paragraph (for insertion into Section 3, Data Use):
"Provider will not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or improve models except to the extent that (a) the data has been irreversibly de-identified in accordance with industry best practices and independently certified as non-identifiable; or (b) the use is limited to aggregated, non-identifying operational telemetry used solely for platform diagnostics, security monitoring, or troubleshooting (\"Operational Diagnostics\"). Provider will not use Customer Data or Derived Data for model training that results in model artifacts shared beyond the Provider’s isolated customer environments without Customer’s prior written consent."

Operational commitments to include as Schedule A:
- Independent privacy review process description and contact.
- Subprocessor notice window: 30 days for new subprocessors with opt-out by written objection.
- Cross-border training: explicit opt-in for any training activities outside the US involving Customer Data.

If ZenPath agrees to the certification + operational schedule, we will create a DocuSign envelope (DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/envelope/ZP-45-2026) and include an execution copy plus the Schedule A.

Thanks — Laura
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Laura / Vivek —

Thanks for the clear, concise language and for including the certifications and Schedule A. ZenPath Legal has reviewed the paragraph and Schedule A and confirms acceptance pending two small edits: (1) replace "irreversibly de-identified" with "de-identified in accordance with NIST SP 800-188 guidelines or equivalent" and (2) add an explicit statement that Derived Data cannot be re-associated with Customer accounts by Provider or its subprocessors.

Assuming those two edits are incorporated, we are ready to sign. Please proceed with the DocuSign envelope; I will coordinate with our GC to execute it today.

Marcus
Head of Security Operations
ZenPath AI
